neighbours.label: owing or repaying an obligation (feel indebted, honor commitments, pay for the use, obligations under a contract)
fire: After all his help, she felt deeply indebted to her neighbour.
A small favour can leave people feeling obliged to return it.
The tenant failed to honor his obligations under the lease.
They should at least repay the kindness they were shown.
We owe our teachers a great debt of gratitude for their patience.
The company must meet its commitments to bondholders by June.
He felt bound to repay the loan before asking for another.
In return for the gift, the family felt they owed the village a feast.
quiet: After all his help, she felt deeply happy with her new garden.
A small favour can make people smile for the rest of the day.
The tenant enjoyed the large windows and the quiet street.
They should at least enjoy the sunshine while it lasts.
We thank our teachers for their patience and good humour.
The company will open its new office downtown by June.
He felt ready to buy a car after saving for a year.
After the festival, the family relaxed and enjoyed the village feast.

notes: top: indebted, obligaciones, give (honor), pay, honore; - pole is enjoy / brag / sit back, the receiving/boasting side
